title: Saga and compensating transactions, where there is no distributed commit

videos.script: Quitanda's checkout touches three services. Stock reserves the coffee, payments charges the card, shipping books the delivery. {{three}} Each has its own database, so there is no single transaction that covers all three. If the delivery cannot be booked, the card has already been charged. {{no-tx}} A saga is the answer the industry settled on: a sequence of local steps, each with a step that undoes it, run in order and undone in reverse when something fails. {{saga}} On your machine you will run the checkout as a saga twice. Once with an orchestrator that calls each service in turn and knows the whole plan. {{orchestration}} And once with no orchestrator at all, where each service reacts to the previous one's events. That is choreography. {{choreography}} You will make each step fail on purpose and watch the compensations run. And you will see the cost that sagas carry and transactions hide: while a saga is half done, other orders can see it. {{isolation}} A reservation that blocks another customer for an order that is about to fail is the price of that, and the lesson shows how to choose who pays it.
